_meta.name: English
_meta.note: Every string a person reads in the window. A new language is a new file beside this one, never a change in code - ADR-21. The keys are English too, and they are what the code refers to.

gui.window.title: Better Windows Services
gui.column.name: Name
gui.columns.hint: Choose what the list shows. Drag a heading to move a column and its edge to resize. What you choose is kept, so the list opens the way you left it.
gui.details.close.hint: Close the panel. Escape does the same, and clears the query when there is no panel.
gui.details.gone: This entry is no longer in the listing, so what is below is the last thing this window read about it.
gui.details.notRead.why: These four are read by a second pass this window does not have, so nobody looked. The command line reads them with bws list --signatures and --memory.
gui.layout.ignored: The kept column layout names columns this window could not use, so they were left out: {0}
gui.layout.noneShown: The kept column layout hides every column, so the usual ones are shown instead.
gui.layout.widths: A kept width could not be read for these columns, so they start where the theme puts them: {0}
gui.layout.unreadable: The kept column layout could not be read, so the usual columns are shown. The file was moved to {1} rather than overwritten. {0}
gui.layout.unreadableStays: The kept column layout could not be read, so the usual columns are shown. It could not be moved out of the way, so this will happen again. {0}
gui.layout.otherSchema: The kept column layout was written against schema version {0} and this program reads version {1}, so it was left alone and the usual columns are shown.
gui.layout.notKept: The column layout was not saved, so this window will open the way it did last time. {0}
gui.layout.noProfile: Windows names no application data folder for this account, so there is nowhere to keep the layout.
gui.search.tip.what: Type a word to search, or write a query: a field, a colon and a value. Put ! in front of a member to exclude it, and give a field twice to mean either.
gui.search.tip.regex: Between slashes it is a regular expression, so /^win.*svc$/ finds names that begin with win and end in svc.
gui.example.shouldBeRunning: Set to start and not running
gui.example.missingFile: The file it runs is not there
gui.filter.hint.adds: Each of these writes what it stands for into the box, so the filter you clicked is a query you can read and edit. Two of these show both.
gui.filter.hint.narrows: Each of these writes what it stands for into the box, so the filter you clicked is a query you can read and edit. Each one narrows the list on its own.
gui.status.failed: Could not read the service control manager. {0}
gui.status.partial: {0} entries were judged on a field that could not be read, so this list may be missing entries, or holding ones that do not belong.
gui.status.tooCostly: The expression ran out of time on {0} entries, so they were never checked. Try a simpler one.
gui.status.holding: The list is holding still while you use it, so nothing joins or leaves under your cursor. It settles when you move away, or on F5.
gui.status.notElevated: Running without administrator rights, so Windows hands over fewer entries than it has.
gui.start.mark.missing: The file this entry is set to launch is not on disk.
gui.start.mark.disabled: Disabled. It will not start, by itself or on request.
gui.start.mark.unknown: The start type could not be read on this account.
gui.against.mark.yes: Set to start automatically and it is not running, and nothing is waiting to start it either.
gui.against.mark.unknown: Whether it matches its start type could not be worked out, because the start type could not be read.
gui.empty.nothingMatched: Nothing on this machine matches what you asked for.
gui.empty.nothingMatchedWayOut: Press Esc to empty the box and see everything again.
gui.empty.nothingToShow: The service control manager handed over no entries at all.
gui.empty.failed: The list could not be read. What went wrong is written under it.
gui.empty.failedWayOut: Press F5 to read the machine again.
gui.query.unreadSignatures: This asks about signatures, which are not read for a listing, so no entry can answer it here. Ask the command line with --signatures.
gui.query.unreadMemory: This asks about memory, which is not read for a listing, so no entry can answer it here. Ask the command line with --memory.
gui.query.unknownField: There is no field called {0}. Fields you can use: {1}.
gui.query.unknownValueNearest: {1} has no value {0}. Did you mean {2}? It accepts: {3}.
gui.query.badPattern: The expression /{0}/ could not be read. {1}
gui.query.unclosedQuote: A quote is opened and never closed, starting at: {0}
gui.query.badNumber: {1} expects a number like 1234, >1000, <500, >=100 or 100-200. It got: {0}
gui.query.emptyTerm: {0} says nothing. A ! needs something after it, and a word needs something in it.
gui.query.patternTooComplex: The wildcard starting {0} has too many parts to build. Use fewer * and ? characters.
gui.query.badSize: {1} expects a size with a unit, like 500MB, >1GB, <100MB or 100MB-1GB. It got: {0}
